description:
Issue summary: Customer (AcmeBank, dedicated pool in us-east-1) reported a gradual throughput decline across their reserved cluster during weekday validation window. Impact: steady p50/p99 degradation for batched routes and higher attach latency leading to request queuing and occasional 429s. Environment: prod us-east-1; dedicated pool reserved for AcmeBank; models in use: redwood-open-gpt-6b for chat and embed-lite-v2 for short embeddings.

Observed behavior: Starting ~2026-03-10 09:15 UTC we see a slow drift in throughput (~10-30% p50 drop) and an increase in attach latency from ~80ms to ~350ms over 40 minutes. No driver crashes or host-level OOMs. Customer traces show a large number of short-lived validation calls from an internal pipeline (model-validation service) that runs on schedule every morning. These validation calls are high-frequency, low-context streams (typically 1-10 tokens) and open/close connections rapidly.

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Run their standard morning validation set against redwood-open-gpt-6b in the dedicated tenant at 09:00 UTC.
2) Observe increased request fanout + short-lived streams; watch p50/p99 throughput and attach latencies in Console.
3) Stopping the validation traffic decreases attach latency and throughput returns to normal over ~10 minutes.

Requested action: Investigate autoscaler behavior and identify mitigation; propose short-term throttle or isolation for the validation loop and longer-term autoscaler/allocator tuning to avoid noisy short-streams from starving GPU attach capacity.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:28 - Aisha Khatri (Customer): We're seeing our production reserved pool slow every morning when validation runs kick off. SDK calls timeout sometimes. Please advise.

2026-03-10 09:40 - Support (Diego Martinez): Thanks Aisha — we've started triage. Can you provide a sample of the validation request pattern (rate per minute, typical payload sizes)? Also confirm if validation runs in parallel with production traffic.

Aisha: It's parallel; roughly 300-500 short requests/min for 20 minutes. Payloads are small (prompt ~30 tokens).

2026-03-10 10:05 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Correlated metrics from us-east-1: high connection churn and a spike in ephemeral session creations from tenant AcmeBank between 09:12-09:32 UTC. Autoscaler scaled GPU count normally but attach success rate dropped; allocator logged ~120 attach retries/min. Links: grafana/redwood/prod/attach-rate (internal).

2026-03-10 11:15 - Support (Diego Martinez): Hypothesis: short-lived validation streams are dominating attach slots and causing allocator to mark capacity as busy, reducing effective throughput for longer-lived batched requests. Working mitigation: temporarily throttle validation traffic at our edge for this tenant. Asked for customer approval to apply soft-rate-limit for 30 minutes.

Aisha: Approved — please proceed.

2026-03-10 11:25 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Applied tenant-level soft throttle (rate-limit = 120 rpm) to model-validation source. Within 3 minutes attach latency started decreasing; by 11:40 UTC throughput recovered to baseline. We'll continue to monitor.
investigation:
Initial data: Console traces + allocator logs + per-tenant connection metrics. Notable findings: (1) Connection churn from validation worker correlated exactly with throughput decline window. (2) Autoscaler did not add extra GPUs because overall token throughput was low — autoscaler heuristics use sustained queue depth and token rates, not short ephemeral stream count. (3) Allocator reported increased attach retries and ephemeral slot hold times due to frequent KV cache warmups on short streams. Hypothesis: high rate of short-lived sessions causes per-attach overhead (context allocation, KV warmup) that reduces effective slot reuse and triggers attach saturation despite nominal free GPU capacity. Tests performed: blocked validation traffic for 15 minutes in canary region -> attach latencies dropped and p50/p99 throughput returned. Microtrace showed numerous prefetch/KV cache churn events during the incident window. Also verified there were no host-level GPU memory pressure or driver errors.

Next steps executed: temporary rate-limit applied to validation origin; cross-team outreach to customer's validation service to add jitter/exponential backoff and increase batch size. Created PR to add autoscaler heuristic to consider short-stream frequency as a factor for scaling decisions. See PR: https://github.com/redwood/serve/pull/4821. Logged linked support items for allocator fairness research.
resolution:
Short-term fix: Applied tenant-level soft throttle on the validation host to limit short validation streams to 120 requests/min for 48h window; immediate improvement observed (attach latency reduced from 350ms -> 85ms, throughput recovered within 10 minutes). Medium-term fix: Merged rate-limiter and backpressure recommendations with customer (validation pipeline patched to batch validations and add jitter). Long-term fix: Merged autoscaler heuristic change to consider ephemeral-stream-rate (PR https://github.com/redwood/serve/pull/4821) and scheduled allocator fairness work to better account for attach cost of short streams.

Follow-ups: 1) SRE to monitor the tenant's attach metrics for two weekly peak windows (assigned to Diego). 2) Product/infra to evaluate a global ephemeral-stream protection (Q2 milestone). 3) CS to confirm with AcmeBank that validation pipeline changes reduce morning spike (Aisha). Postmortem draft created: https://confluence.redwood.internal/dedicated-autoscale-postmortem/SUP-555321.
